set.body:
Scheduling lane: closed. Governing plan: docs/refactor/PLAN.md.

Current disposition, 2026-09-19: Decision recorded in PLAN section 2 and ADR 0019: one reviewed committed JSON admission authority, with byte verification and bound record identity; arbitrary caller JSON is not trusted. Implementation remains on bd-01M2WTGF981AY7RCN8QC42JSPT.

Historical finding and scope retained below; current acceptance ownership above governs.

OWNER DECISION. How are the three byte hashes pinned: the annotation sha256 and the part A and part B sha256?

Today it is effectively TWO KEYS. The hashes are written in docs/data/sherlock/timebase-repair.json AND as Scala literals in MediaManifest.nn2017 (SherlockAnnotations.scala:45-67), and since 0315bd6a / 41c1338f a test requires the two to agree. Admitting different bytes means changing both.

- ONE KEY: MediaManifest reads the hashes from the committed record like every other derived constant. The protection is git review of the committed record, which is how source-manifest.json already works everywhere else in intake. Consistent; one place to change.
- TWO KEYS: keep the literals as admission pins beside the record, test-bound. A second lock, at the cost of a second copy of an identity -- the pattern the intake epic otherwise removes.

Author's lean: one key, for consistency. It is a policy call about ADMISSION, so it is the owner's. It overlaps bd-01M1CQ2H7VPSKRT02M5H7HN1K6 item B0 (Sherlock artifact-specific admission; owner codex-storymodel4s-sherlock-intake; cand-6P2D7ZBV13BRD1XQ791PB3GCC5), whose "artifact-binding receipt must establish media, annotation, recall, alias and timebase identities". Decide there or here, but decide once.

NOT part of this decision: durations, tick rate, run boundary, row count and part ids are MEASUREMENTS. They move to the record regardless (sibling record bead).
set.title: C1 DECISION (owner): admission hashes -- one key (read from timebase-repair.json) or two keys (JSON plus a test-bound Scala literal)
